## Terraform Provider for SAP Integration Suite v0.8.0

### Overview

0.8.0 completes Security Content: CA-signed certificate chains for key pairs,
PGP keys and the custom parameters of OAuth2 client credentials. With them, a
tenant's keys and credentials can be kept in the same configuration as the
integration content that uses them.

All three are unofficial. Their requests are known only from the tenant
`$metadata`, not from SAP's documentation, so they need
`enable_unofficial = true`. Each one passed an acceptance test on a tenant.

Integration Assessment moves the other way: SAP's Entities API specification
documents the requests of its resources and data sources, so they are now
supported and no longer need an opt-in switch.

### Highlights

- **CA-signed key pairs.** `sapintegrationsuite_key_pair` has
  `certificate_signing_request`, the PEM CSR to have signed.
  `sapintegrationsuite_key_pair_certificate_chain` uploads the signed
  certificate with the certificates that issued it, in any order and with or
  without the root. It reads the chain back, refuses a private key pasted into
  the chain, and imports by the key pair's alias.
- **PGP keys.** `sapintegrationsuite_pgp_public_key` and
  `sapintegrationsuite_pgp_secret_key` hold one key each in the tenant's
  public or secret keyring, for the PGP encryptor, decryptor, signer and
  verifier steps. The plan shows the key ID and fingerprint, computed locally.
  The secret key and its passphrase are write-only.
- **OAuth2 custom parameters.**
  `sapintegrationsuite_oauth2_client_credential` manages `custom_parameters`:
  key, value and whether SAP sends the parameter in the body, as a header or in
  the URL. Without the attribute, the plan of an update warns when SAP holds
  parameters set in its UI.
- **Integration Assessment without opt-in.** Vendors, applications, application
  instances, technologies, technology instances, technology profile entries and
  the taxonomy are supported. Only a link change in place stays unofficial,
  because the specification's update bodies list no links.

```terraform
provider "sapintegrationsuite" {
  enable_unofficial = true
  # ...
}

resource "sapintegrationsuite_pgp_public_key" "partner" {
  public_key = file("${path.module}/keys/partner-public.asc")
}

resource "sapintegrationsuite_oauth2_client_credential" "graph" {
  id                = "GRAPH_OAUTH"
  token_service_url = "https://login.example.com/oauth2/v2.0/token"
  client_id         = "integration-client"

  custom_parameters = [
    { key = "resource", value = "https://graph.example.com", send_as_part_of = "body" },
  ]

  client_secret_wo         = var.backend_client_secret
  client_secret_wo_version = "1"
}
```

### Breaking changes

None.

### Upgrading from 0.7

- No state migration.
- A configuration that sets `enable_unofficial = true` only for Integration
  Assessment can drop it, unless it changes a link in place. Such a plan fails
  without the switch and names it; nothing is replaced.
- `certificate_signing_request` of `sapintegrationsuite_key_pair` is read only
  with `enable_unofficial = true`.

The Provider Upgrades guide on the Terraform Registry describes each step.

### Known limitations

- SAP has no request that removes a certificate chain from a key pair, so
  destroying the chain resource leaves the chain in place.
- SAP signs a key pair's CSR anew after a chain upload. The provider keeps the
  stored text while subject and public key stay the same.
- SAP takes OAuth2 custom parameters only when a credential is created and
  deletes them with every update. With `custom_parameters` set, every change
  replaces the credential, a secret rotation included.
- PGP keys cover the Cloud runtime only. SAP deletes a key's public and secret
  part together, so the public key resource leaves a key with a secret part in
  place on destroy.
- A PGP key ID that exists already fails the create; import it instead.

### SAP API references

- Unofficial, known only from the tenant `$metadata`: the key pair's
  `SigningRequest`, `CertificateChainResources`, `PgpKeyringPublicResources`,
  `PgpKeyringSecretResources`, `PgpKeyEntries` and `CustomParameters` of OAuth2
  client credentials. Tenant probes and acceptance tests confirmed how they
  behave.
- Integration Assessment Entities API specification (Business Accelerator Hub):
  the entity sets and requests of the Integration Assessment resources and data
  sources.

### Compatibility

- Terraform 1.5 or later; 1.11 or later for resources with write-only
  attributes (`*_wo`).
- Terraform plugin protocol 6.
